findings.title: totalPages off by one for exact multiples of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50) it reports 2 pages instead of 1, so `showingLast` is false and the 'next' control is enabled, paging to an empty member list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by client
findings.body: Group#asJSON in the JS model posts `name`, `alias_level` and `visible` to POST /admin/groups, but the `create` action only reads `name` and `visible`. A newly created group silently loses the chosen alias level (it stays at the default) until the user saves again, which is confusing and inconsistent with `update`.

findings.title: visible forced to false when param absent
findings.body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` in both create and update sets visible to false whenever the param is missing (e.g. a partial update or an API client that omits it), silently hiding the group. Only assign when `params.key?(:visible)`.

findings.title: members endpoint accepts unbounded limit
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly in the query with no upper bound, so any user can request e.g. `?limit=1000000` and force serialization of every group member in one request. Clamp the limit (e.g. `[limit, 100].min`) and guard against negative values.

findings.title: remove_member always reports success even if user is not a member
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` relies on passing a raw id to the has_many collection and gives no indication whether anything was removed; a bogus or non-member user_id returns 200 success. Consider looking the user up / deleting the GroupUser record explicitly and returning a 404/422 when no membership existed, so the UI doesn't show a false success.

findings.title: remove_member test uses wrong HTTP verb and hardcoded automatic group id
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the only route for that action is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members, so the test does not exercise the real routing. It also assumes group id 1 is automatic, which is fragile; fabricate an automatic group instead. Same hardcoded-id issue in the add_members example.

findings.title: No spec for new paginated GroupsController#members response
findings.body: The members endpoint changed from a bare serialized array to `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` with pagination applied to all groups (previously only automatic ones). There is no spec covering the new payload shape, limit/offset behaviour, or the total count, so regressions in the contract consumed by the JS model would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Non-block {{each}} with keyword binding and no closing tag
findings.body: `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` mixes the `x in y` keyword form (which requires a block, `{{#each}}...{{/each}}`) with the legacy non-block itemView form. In Ember 1.x this either throws a compile error or renders nothing, so the member list would not display. Use `{{each members itemView="group-member"}}` (and reference `this` in the item template) or a proper block form.
